title: MATH GAOKAO - 399
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Find a specified term of an arithmetic sequence using the first term and common difference.
questions.question: In an arithmetic sequence, \(a_1=3\) and the common difference is \(d=4\). What is \(a_{10}\)?
questions.explanation:
Use the formula for the nth term of an arithmetic sequence:
\[
a_n=a_1+(n-1)d
\]
Substitute \(a_1=3\), \(d=4\), and \(n=10\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{10}&=3+(10-1)(4) \\
&=3+36 \\
&=39
\end{aligned}
\]
So the correct value is \(39\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the first term of an arithmetic sequence from two given terms.
questions.question: In an arithmetic sequence, \(a_3=10\) and \(a_7=26\). Find the first term \(a_1\).
questions.explanation:
The difference between the 7th and 3rd terms is
\[
a_7-a_3=(7-3)d=4d
\]
So
\[
26-10=4d \implies 16=4d \implies d=4
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_1&=a_3-2d \\
&=10-2(4) \\
&=2
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the first term is \(2\).
questions.hint: The difference between two terms equals the difference of their indices times the common difference.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the sum of the first \(n\) terms of an arithmetic sequence.
questions.question: Find the sum of the first \(20\) terms of the arithmetic sequence \(5,9,13,\ldots\).
questions.explanation:
Here \(a_1=5\), \(d=4\), and \(n=20\). Use
\[
S_n=\frac{n}{2}\left[2a_1+(n-1)d\right]
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_{20}&=\frac{20}{2}\left[2(5)+19(4)\right] \\
&=10(10+76)=10(86)=860
\end{aligned}
\]
So the sum is \(860\).

questions.concept: Number of Terms in an Arithmetic Sequence
questions.learningObjective: Determine how many terms belong to a finite arithmetic sequence.
questions.question: How many terms are in the arithmetic sequence \(7,11,15,\ldots,99\)?
questions.explanation:
The sequence has first term \(a_1=7\) and common difference \(d=4\). Its nth term is
\[
a_n=7+(n-1)(4)
\]
Set this equal to the last term \(99\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
7+4(n-1)&=99 \\
4(n-1)&=92 \\
n-1&=23 \\
n&=24
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the sequence contains \(24\) terms.
questions.hint: Set the general term equal to the last term and solve for \(n\).

questions.learningObjective: Count integers divisible by one of two numbers using inclusion-exclusion.
questions.question: How many integers from \(1\) to \(120\), inclusive, are divisible by \(3\) or \(5\)?
questions.explanation:
There are \(120/3=40\) multiples of \(3\) and \(120/5=24\) multiples of \(5\). Their overlap consists of \(120/15=8\) multiples of \(15\). Inclusion-exclusion therefore gives
\[
40+24-8=56.
\]
The distractor \(64\) counts the overlap twice.
questions.hint: Count multiples of \(3\), multiples of \(5\), and subtract those counted twice.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the first term of an arithmetic sequence that is divisible by a given integer.
questions.question: For the arithmetic sequence \(a_n=4n+3\), which term is the first one divisible by \(5\)?
questions.explanation:
Check the first few terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_1&=4(1)+3=7 \\
a_2&=4(2)+3=11 \\
a_3&=4(3)+3=15
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(15\) is divisible by \(5\), and \(7\) and \(11\) are not, the first such term is the 3rd term.
questions.hint: Check terms in order or solve \(4n+3\equiv 0\pmod 5\).

questions.learningObjective: Find the smallest index for which an arithmetic sequence term exceeds a given value.
questions.question: In the arithmetic sequence \(a_n=3n-1\), find the smallest \(n\) for which \(a_n>100\).
questions.explanation:
We need
\[
3n-1>100
\]
\[
3n>101
\]
\[
n>\frac{101}{3}\approx 33.67
\]
The smallest integer \(n\) satisfying this is \(34\). Indeed,
\[
a_{34}=3(34)-1=101>100
\]
while
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{33}&=3(33)-1 \\
&=98 \\
&\le 100
\end{aligned}
\]
So the answer is \(34\).
questions.hint: Solve the inequality and round up to the next integer.

questions.learningObjective: Count multiples of a given integer between two bounds using an arithmetic sequence.
questions.question: How many multiples of \(7\) are between \(100\) and \(500\) inclusive?
questions.explanation:
The smallest multiple of \(7\) that is at least \(100\) is
\[
105=7\cdot 15
\]
The largest multiple of \(7\) that is at most \(500\) is
\[
497=7\cdot 71
\]
The multiples are \(7\cdot 15, 7\cdot 16,\ldots,7\cdot 71\). The number of integers from \(15\) to \(71\) inclusive is
\[
71-15+1=57
\]
So there are \(57\) multiples.
questions.hint: Write the multiples as \(7k\) and count the possible integer values of \(k\).

questions.concept: Term from Sum of an Arithmetic Sequence
questions.learningObjective: Find a term of an arithmetic sequence from a given sum formula.
questions.question: The sum of the first \(n\) terms of an arithmetic sequence is \(S_n=n^2+3n\). Find the 10th term \(a_{10}\).
questions.explanation:
For \(n\ge 2\), the nth term satisfies
\[
a_n=S_n-S_{n-1}
\]
Thus
\[
a_{10}=S_{10}-S_9
\]
Compute:
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_{10}&=10^2+3(10) \\
&=100+30 \\
&=130
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_9&=9^2+3(9) \\
&=81+27 \\
&=108
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
a_{10}=130-108=22
\]
So the 10th term is \(22\).

questions.learningObjective: Count how many terms of an arithmetic sequence are divisible by a given integer.
questions.question: In the arithmetic sequence \(3,10,17,\ldots\), how many of the first \(100\) terms are divisible by \(5\)?
questions.explanation:
The first term is \(3\) and the common difference is \(7\), so the nth term is
\[
a_n=3+(n-1)(7)=7n-4
\]
We need \(a_n\) to be divisible by \(5\):
\[
7n-4\equiv 0\pmod 5
\]
Since \(7\equiv 2\pmod 5\),
\[
2n-4\equiv 0\pmod 5
\]
\[
2n\equiv 4\pmod 5
\]
Multiplying by the inverse of \(2\) modulo \(5\), which is \(3\), gives
\[
n\equiv 12\equiv 2\pmod 5
\]
So \(n=2,7,12,\ldots,97\) within the first \(100\) terms. The number of such values is
\[
\frac{97-2}{5}+1=19+1=20
\]
Therefore, \(20\) of the first \(100\) terms are divisible by \(5\).
questions.hint: Find the general term of the sequence and solve the divisibility congruence modulo \(5\).
